title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{R})^\sim$ is the universal cover of $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Its maximal compact $SO(2)\simeq\mathbb{U}$ lifts to $\mathbb{R}$ via $t\mapsto \exp 2i\pi t$. $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim$ is the preimage of $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, a central extension $1\to\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim\to\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})\to1$. The kernel is generated by $\omega_0'$, the lift of the full $2\pi$ rotation. In $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, $\rho$ has order 6 and $\sigma$ has order 4, with $\rho^3=\sigma^2=-1$.

Step 1 (end of the lemma from p. 763). If $\zeta=\mu_n\subset\mathbb{U}$, then $\tilde\zeta=\{t: nt\in\mathbb{Z}\}=\frac1n\mathbb{Z}\simeq\mathbb{Z}$. So preimages of finite cyclic subgroups are infinite cyclic.

Step 2 (Corollary). Lifts $\tilde\rho,\tilde\sigma$ exist with $\tilde\rho^3=\tilde\sigma^{-2}$. Both sides lift $-1$, so they differ by some $\omega_0'^k$. Changing the lifts by $\omega_0'^a,\omega_0'^b$ changes the defect by $3a+2b$. Since $\gcd(2,3)=1$ this can always be killed. The solutions form a $\mathbb{Z}$-torsor (18).

Step 3. Rigidification. The preimage of the centre $\{\pm1\}$ is monogenic $\simeq\mathbb{Z}$; it is the lift of rotation by $\pi$. It has a unique generator $\omega_0$ with $\omega_0^2=\omega_0'$ (19). One then asks for $\tilde\rho^3=\omega_0^{-1}$ and $\tilde\sigma^2=\omega_0$ (20).
- Concretely, in the $t$-coordinate: $\tilde\rho\leftrightarrow t=-1/6$, $\tilde\sigma\leftrightarrow t=1/4$, $\omega_0\leftrightarrow 1/2$.
- These lifts are now unique: $(\tilde\rho\,\omega_0'^a)^3=\omega_0^{-1}\omega_0^{6a}$ forces $a=0$, and similarly for $\sigma$.

Purpose. This prepares a presentation of $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim\simeq\langle\tilde\rho,\tilde\sigma\mid\tilde\rho^3=\tilde\sigma^{-2}\rangle\simeq B_3$ (trefoil group). Here $\omega_0$ corresponds to $\Delta^{\pm2}$, the generator of the centre of $B_3$, and $\omega_0'$ to $\Delta^{\pm4}$. On the next pages it is extended to $\mathrm{Gl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim$ via an order-2 lift $\tilde\tau$ of a reflection. All this belongs to the Longue Marche treatment of the 'Teichmüller tower' at genus 0/1, with the action of complex conjugation.
errors: Sign inconsistency between (17) and (18). With the normalization $\tilde\rho^3=\tilde\sigma^{-2}$, replacing $(\tilde\rho,\tilde\sigma)$ by $(\tilde\rho\omega_0'^{2n},\tilde\sigma\omega_0'^{3n})$ multiplies the left side by $\omega_0'^{6n}$ and the right side by $\omega_0'^{-6n}$, so the relation breaks for $n\neq0$. The torsor action should be $(\tilde\rho\omega_0'^{2n},\tilde\sigma\omega_0'^{-3n})$. Alternatively (18) is correct for the relation $\tilde\rho^3=\tilde\sigma^{2}$. The margin note 'Faire la vérification' suggests Grothendieck had not yet checked this.

Minor: (20) is consistent with (17), since $\tilde\rho^3=\omega_0^{-1}=\tilde\sigma^{-2}$. Uniqueness in (20) holds, but the existence argument is only sketched ('résulte aussitôt de la prop. précédente').

ideas.what: Preimage of a finite cyclic subgroup $\mu_n\subset SO(2)$ in the universal cover of $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ is $\frac1n\mathbb{Z}\simeq\mathbb{Z}$
ideas.modern_name: Lifting torsion to the universal cover $\widetilde{SL_2(\mathbb{R})}$ (torsion-freeness of $\widetilde{SL_2}$)

ideas.what: Presentation of $\mathrm{Sl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim$ by lifts $\tilde\rho,\tilde\sigma$ with $\tilde\rho^3=\tilde\sigma^{-2}$, the set of such lifts being a $\mathbb{Z}$-torsor
ideas.modern_name: $\widetilde{SL_2(\mathbb{Z})}\cong B_3\cong$ trefoil knot group $\langle x,y\mid x^3=y^2\rangle$
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Artin; Milnor, 'Introduction to Algebraic K-theory' 1971 / Brieskorn manifolds 1975; Serre, Trees)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$, $B_3$ and the genus 0/1 Teichmüller groups in general terms; this explicit lift computation is not known to me in his published texts

ideas.what: Canonical square root $\omega_0$ of the kernel generator $\omega_0'$, lifting $-1$, used to normalize the lifts uniquely: $\tilde\rho^3=\omega_0^{-1}$, $\tilde\sigma^2=\omega_0$
ideas.modern_name: Centre of $B_3$ generated by $\Delta^2=(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^3=(\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1)^2$; kernel of $B_3\to SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by $\Delta^4$

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, routine computation of the well-known central extension $\widetilde{SL_2(\mathbb{Z})}\cong B_3$ with canonically normalized lifts of the torsion generators. Its only interest is as a preparatory step toward $\mathrm{Gl}(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim$ with complex conjugation on the following pages. It contains a small sign slip in the torsor action (18). Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'le groupe des ces $t$ est $\simeq\mathbb{Z}$, cqfd' (not 'des cas').

In (17)–(20) the image clearly shows tildes on $\rho,\sigma$, and $\omega_0'$ (primed) as the canonical generator of the kernel of $Sl(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim\to Sl(2,\mathbb{Z})$; (19) reads $\omega_0^2=\omega_0'$.
Inserted phrase above the line: 'l'image inverse des centres $\{\pm1\}$' rather than 'l'image des centres'.

Bottom-left margin is roughly: 'Comme on a déjà dit : $\widetilde{\{\pm1\}}$ est un groupe monogène ... l'image inverse de $\{\pm1\}$ dans $Sl(2,\mathbb{Z})^\sim$ ... (comp. les relèvements de $\rho,\sigma$), et on a alors les relations (20)'. Several words are uncertain.
Top-left margin: 'pour une démonstration plus symétrique, voir (20) plus bas'.
